mechanism_narrative: The week-over-week decline in RETAIL_REC has accelerated each of the last three weeks (-25.7 to -59.9), indicating a self-reinforcing momentum of reduced discretionary activity that will persist into the next four weeks absent any countervailing signal.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -25.7 to -59.9 over four weeks with increasing weekly decrements
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite the prior three weeks showing accelerating decline.

mechanism_narrative: Once RESIDENTIAL mobility crosses +15 points above baseline, it signals binding stay-at-home policy enforcement has reached a compliance threshold, which mechanically suppresses RETAIL_REC further over the following one to two weeks as non-essential movement is curtailed.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 19.4 at t-0w, crossing the 15-point threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline further in the week following a RESIDENTIAL reading above +15, or rebounds within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Joint sharp declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate collapsing commuting infrastructure usage and office attendance; when both fall by more than 10 points week-on-week simultaneously, the compounded reduction in daily out-of-home routines drives a larger-than-additive drop in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, since retail trips are often chained to commute paths.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall more than 10 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 11.9 points and WORKPLACES fell 7.1 points from t-2w to t-1w, both continuing to fall from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is proportionally no larger than the sum of individual TRANSIT and WORKPLACES declines would predict, or RETAIL_REC stabilizes despite joint commuting-series collapse.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, the collapse of PARKS mobility (from -3.1 to -32.4 over three weeks) signals that outdoor recreation itself is being curtailed by policy, not just weather; this policy-driven suppression spills over to retail and recreation venues, continuing to depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as enforcement broadens.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -3.1 at t-3w to -32.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC flattens or rises over the next two weeks even as PARKS continues to decline, indicating decoupling from the policy-driven outdoor restriction mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The deceleration in GROCERY_PHARM's rate of decline relative to RETAIL_REC's rate of decline (GROCERY_PHARM fell only 8 points over four weeks versus RETAIL_REC's 34-point fall) suggests households have completed initial panic-stocking behavior and are stabilizing essential trips; this stabilization pattern typically precedes a floor effect in overall out-of-home activity, allowing RETAIL_REC decline to decelerate within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined only from -9.1 to -23.4 while RETAIL_REC declined from -25.7 to -59.9 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's weekly decline rate continues to accelerate rather than decelerate over the next four weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM stabilizing.

mechanism_narrative: The steep PARKS decline despite no natural seasonal reason for reduced outdoor desirability (data trend is inconsistent with typical seasonal recreation patterns) indicates an artificial, policy-driven override of seasonal behavior; this override extends to retail venues, continuing to pull RETAIL_REC down for the next four weeks as the artificial suppression dominates any seasonal pull toward increased outdoor/retail activity.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS mobility turned sharply negative (-32.4) despite no seasonal basis for reduced park usage
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks while PARKS remains suppressed, indicating the seasonal/policy override mechanism does not transmit to retail behavior.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility week-on-week reflects entrenching stay-home behavioral norms; as households adapt routines (grocery delivery, remote work), the behavioral substitution away from retail trips strengthens, producing a continued one-week-ahead decline in RETAIL_REC that tracks the RESIDENTIAL increase almost one-to-one.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose each week from 8.7 to 19.4 while RETAIL_REC fell each week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week even though RESIDENTIAL continues its weekly increase, breaking the inverse co-movement pattern.

mechanism_narrative: If the week-on-week magnitude of RETAIL_REC decline shrinks for two consecutive weeks (deceleration of the decline rate, e.g., from a 12-point drop to a 6-point drop), this signals an approaching behavioral floor where further mobility reduction becomes physically or economically infeasible, causing RETAIL_REC to flatten or mildly reverse upward within the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: weekly decline in RETAIL_REC shrinks for two consecutive weeks relative to the prior week's decline magnitude
evidence_refs: fact:weekly declines were -6.2, -12.2, -15.8 points, showing acceleration rather than deceleration as of t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline at an accelerating or stable rate over the next four weeks even after two consecutive weeks of decelerating decline are observed.
